Virtual BMW X9 Doesn't Care About the Mercedes GLS or Audi Q7, Instead Targets Q9 and Caddy Escalade
14 photos
Photo: carlchan100 / Instagram
The premium Bavarian automaker BMW has prepared a ton of new stuff going into 2027 – but we’re not sure that a flagship crossover SUV larger than the current X7 is also on the menu. But the parallel universes of vehicular CGI seem to think so.
The global luxury crown belongs to BMW, and you can’t hold on to the throne without breaking a sweat – BMW has been on top of the charts above Mercedes-Benz since 2021 and has no intention of vacating the premises. As such, it’s no wonder that a lot of novelties are coming next year.
The list includes a new entry-level EV , the potential BMW i1 hatchback with a short rear and Neue Klasse attire; the reworked X1 and iX1 base crossover SUVs; minor updates for the X2 and iX2 crossover coupe-SUVs; the station wagon version of the new electric 3 Series; the M3 and the first all-electric M3 ; an X3 M with electricity along with an iX4 M; the mid-cycle refresh of the 5 Series; and the switch to electricity of the iX7 plus the new BMW Alpina 7 Series as a rival for Maybach.
It’s pretty hard to also cram a flagship BMW X9 in there in the real world, so leave it to the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to fill in the blanks. For example, Carl Chan, an MA in Intelligent Mobility from the Royal College of Art in London, the UK, is also known as ' carlchan100 ' on social media because of things like this unofficial, hypothetical design project.
His vision of the BMW X9 ultra-luxury full-size three-row crossover SUV is pretty simple and mindful – a combination of the current BMW X7’s split headlights and a large kidney grille with elements taken from the Neue Klasse but adapted for a more elegant posture. The SUV is also pretty muscular, with a massive shoulder line to give it the look of a widebody model, especially above the rear fenders.
Around the back, the Neue Klasse LED taillights are more than obvious, along with a sculpted bumper to add precious inches to the crumple zones. There’s also a full-length panoramic glass roof, but even so we can’t see inside the cockpit because there’s no accompanying rendering from the pixel master. So, what do you think – cool or not?
As for the rumor mill, the latest reports on the whereabouts of the potential BMW X9 discuss about a combination of the Neue Klasse design and the enhanced CLAR architecture to allow for the massive SUV built in America to include powerful gasoline engines and satisfy the current adversity for EVs. So, is this a good rival for the Audi Q9 and the Cadillac Escalade? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Carl Chan (@carlchan100)
